messages:
maria: Heads up — prod-ap-southeast1 is showing a sustained spike of GPU-pending pods (tiny workloads). Seen ~120 pending for 30m :confused:
kai: link to grafana? which metric is peaking? :eyes:
maria: grafana -> cluster/allocations -> gpu_pending_count, + pod_size_histogram. quick numbers: pending=120, tiny_pods(<1GPU)=62% of queue, evictions up 5x in last hour.
lucas: did the new label/taint rollout happen last deploy? small pods might be getting stuck due to strict nodeAffinity/taints. can you paste `kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep Pending`?
maria: pasted snippet in thread (truncated):
```
# kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending
ml-train-xyz-0           Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
rerank-worker-abcd       Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu
tiny-batch-123           Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector
```
ana: saw the autoscaler logs around 02:10 UTC — scale-up attempted but hit quota/CP limit for ap-southeast1. Controller error: `InsufficientCapacity: requested 4 gpus but region quota allows 2`. Also noticed the new taint `gpu:dedicated=true:NoSchedule` landed yesterday during label rollout.
infra-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-ap-southeast1 threshold breached (count=120) at 1799501100
kai: mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: patch small batch pods to tolerate the `gpu:dedicated=true:NoSchedule` taint OR relax nodeSelector 2) scale a small spot pool in the region (if quota allows) 3) enable binpack coalescing for fractional requests.
lucas: caution — tolerating that taint will mix tiny jobs into dedicated racks and could spike cross-az egress if those nodes are in different AZs. Cost could jump. But it's acceptable short-term.
maria: quick patch command I used (example):
```
kubectl patch pod tiny-batch-123 -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu","operator":"Equal","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
ana: I requested quota bump with cloud-ops (ticket #CLOUD-9234). In the meantime I scaled the provisioner deployment from 2 -> 4 replicas: `kubectl scale deploy gpu-provisioner -n infra --replicas=4` — started a background scale job, will monitor.
ops-bot: Deployment gpu-provisioner scaled from 2 to 4 replicas by ana at 1799501165. JobID=scale-1799501165
maria: after patching tolerations + provisioner bump we saw pending drop to ~18 and evictions tail off. Backfill started, but noticed a short-lived cost bump in the AZ (estimated +8% infra spend for last hour).
kai: long-term actions (assigned to infra-scheduler): - implement small-pod packing optimizer (coalesce fractional requests) - add an exception in rollout process to avoid `gpu:dedicated` taint during high-util windows - reduce lease TTL to allow faster rebalancing - add autoscaler fallback to other regions before marking pods evict.
lucas: can we also add a Canary for label/taint rollouts: gate if pending_gpus > 20 for 15m. prevents this class of regressions.
maria: agreed. i'll open an infra ticket and add the rollback playbook notes. created ticket INFRA-2049 with runbook snippet.
ana: current status: pending=12, backfill progressing. keeping autoscaler quota ticket pinned.
kai: thanks team — follow-up: please post postmortem/update in #eng-infra when INFRA-2049 has runbook + timeline. I'll add to next weekly ops review. :thumbsup:
